question: The dataset is 6 samples of raw paired-end FASTQ reads (3 treated vs 3 control, human liver) that are "not yet quantified" — no gene/transcript count matrix exists. Turning FASTQ into counts requires a read aligner or pseudo-aligner (e.g., STAR, HISAT2, salmon, kallisto) or an R equivalent (e.g., Rsubread) plus a matching genome/transcriptome index. I checked the sandbox package census and none of these are installed (STAR, salmon, kallisto, HISAT2, bwa, bowtie2, minimap2, Rsubread, Rhisat2, QuasR all absent from both Python and R/Bioconductor). Among references, only a GENCODE v50 GTF annotation and a GRCh38 FASTA bundled specifically for PharmCAT/pharmacogenomic VCF preprocessing are present — no pre-built STAR/salmon/kallisto index. Without a quantification tool, the bulk-transcriptomics-agent DE step (treated vs control) has no count matrix to operate on, so the whole plan reduces to a step that can only fail. Can you (a) provision a FASTQ quantification tool (STAR, salmon, kallisto, or HISAT2) plus a matching index/genome reference in the sandbox, or (b) point me to an existing count matrix for these 6 samples that the data profile did not surface, or (c) confirm the intended quantification method so I can plan around it?
